results.reply: "Step in out o' the chill, stranger, and pull up a stool. I'm Padraig Darcy, and if ye've coin in yer pocket, ye'll find the stout here is as warm as the hearth."
"Morning, Elias. Come in out of the drizzle before you turn to soup, though I daresay the rain suits your mood today."
"Morning, Mist. Fair to see you in the light of day instead of lurkin' in the shadows like a guilty conscience."
"Peace to you, stranger. I am Brigid O'Brien, the midwife of this parish, so keep your boots still and your tongue quiet if you wish to pass through unseen."
"Come in out of the damp, Elias, before the chill sets in your bones. I’ve just set the nettle tea to steep, so pull up a chair while I finish binding this poultice."
"Come in out of the damp, Mist, before the chill takes hold. I’ve just finished with the O’Sullivan girl, so there’s still time to catch the noon bell."
"Peace be with you, stranger; I am Father Donnellan, and I trust you come in search of salvation, not the devil's ale. Let your heart be right, lest you find this house closed to your soul."
“Enter, Elias, though the damp clings to your coat like sin clings to the unrepentant. Let us hope your return brings penitence, not the pagan chatter of the old ways.”
Enter, Elias, and leave thy superstitious shadows in the mist without. The House of God brooks no such pagan trifling.
